system.name: ReSim
system.one_liner: A controllable driving world model trained on expert plus simulated non-expert data to simulate reliable futures under any ego action, with a Video2Reward module.

content.variant_note: three lettered bands: data sources fan in, a Prior Work versus ReSim comparison in the middle, three applications fan out
content.argues: Adding simulated non-expert driving data lets a world model follow even hazardous actions where expert-only models fail, and its simulated futures support policy planning, selection and closed-loop simulation.
content.subject: Three data-source cards, a prior-work versus ReSim simulation lane ending in Video2Reward, and three application cards with small bar charts.

lessons.what_to_learn: Tie data, method and applications together with colour: give each data source a colour and numeral on its card, carry it onto the database icons that feed the model, and draw the baseline as a grey lane above the coloured proposed lane with the same slots; end with small icon-story cards for the downstream uses.
lessons.suits: World-model, generative or data-mixture papers whose story is which data go in, how outputs differ from a baseline and what the model enables downstream.

evidence: (a) Heterogeneous driving data includes (i,ii) experts’ safe driving logs, and (iii) potentially dangerous (non-expert) driving behaviors from simulations.
prior works like Vista [16] fail to follow the specified steering action, while ReSim accurately simulates off-road behaviors.
we develop a Video2Reward model to convert simulated video outputs from ReSim into scalar rewards in real-world scenarios.

summary: ReSim is a controllable driving world model trained on real expert driving videos plus non-expert data from a simulator so that it can simulate reliable futures even for hazardous ego actions, with a Video2Reward module that scores simulated futures. Figure 1 has three lettered bands separated by dashed rules. (a) shows three tinted data cards (universal driving videos, expert data, non-expert simulated data), each with frame pairs, an ego-car action diagram and a numbered database icon. (b) compares a grey Prior Work lane trained on sources i and ii with a blue ReSim lane trained on i to iii, each producing a frame strip under the same left-turn command, and ends with a Video2Reward funnel and trophy. (c) gives three application cards, two with small PDMS bar charts.
